title: QUIC ERR_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT with HAProxy 3.2.x
body: I intermittently get ERR_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT when forcing HTTP/3 with curl against HAProxy 3.2.x. A request normally completes over HTTP/3, but roughly one out of every 10-20 attempts hangs until the handshake times out. I captured packet traces from working and hanging sessions.

symptoms_visible: When I repeatedly force HTTP/3 with curl, about one attempt in every 10-20 hangs and ends in ERR_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT; the other attempts complete normally over HTTP/3.
N0.label: N0 intermittent QUIC handshake timeout reported

symptoms_visible: The intermittent curl handshake timeout is unchanged after I try higher QUIC frame-loss and reorder-ratio tuning values.
N1_x.label: N1_x QUIC loss tuning aftermath

symptoms_visible: The timeout reproduces against multiple servers and over DSL, Starlink, and fiber connections, on both IPv4 and IPv6.
During a hanging attempt, my QUIC trace logs 'packet parsing failed -> dropped' for an Initial packet.
N1.label: N1 lower-layer QUIC trace collected

symptoms_visible: Curl still intermittently hangs when I test with UDP GSO disabled in HAProxy.
An affected Firefox user no longer sees hanging connections while HTTP/3 is disabled.
N2.label: N2 transport toggles tested

symptoms_visible: The supplied static curl builds do not reproduce the hang locally, in the same rack, remotely, or on my Mac.
With otherwise comparable custom curl builds, the build using ngtcp2 reproduces the timeout while the build using OpenSSL QUIC does not.
N3.label: N3 client build comparison completed

symptoms_visible: After deploying the ncbuf2 development build, my repeated curl loop succeeds and our previously affected user reports no hangs over the weekend.
N4_x.label: N4_x initial ncbuf2 candidate aftermath

symptoms_visible: The corrected ncbmbuf build is running on all our machines and remains stable; users who previously saw the problem can no longer reproduce hangs in Firefox or Edge.
N5.label: N5 corrected ncbmbuf build verified

symptoms_visible: With the corrected QUIC buffer implementation, repeated HTTP/3 curl requests complete and our Firefox and Edge users no longer encounter the hanging connections.
N_terminal.label: terminal corrected QUIC buffer fix merged and verified

solution.intent: Treat the failures as ordinary QUIC packet loss or reordering and increase HAProxy's frame-loss and reorder tolerance.
solution.concrete_example: Increase tune.quic.max-frame-loss and tune.quic.reorder-ratio, then repeat the HTTP/3 curl loop.

edges.comment: Reporter c2 on the reporter's HAProxy deployment: tune.quic.max-frame-loss=40 and tune.quic.reorder-ratio=60 were actually tried, with the same intermittent timeout.

question_patterns: Can you capture lower-layer QUIC traces during a hanging attempt rather than only HTTP/3 traces?
Please enable the QUIC trace source, reproduce one timeout, and paste the relevant raw lines.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I attached the QUIC trace. Around the failure it prints 'qc_parse_pkt_frms(): leaving on error' followed by 'packet parsing failed -> dropped' for an Initial packet with pn=2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The QUIC trace shows the Initial packets arriving and being processed without any parsing error or dropped packet; the connection stalls later after the handshake completes.
The same parsing-failed and dropped-packet lines appear for a different Initial packet number.

edges.comment: Participant2 c3 requested lower-layer traces; reporter c4 supplied raw QUIC log lines from the reporter's VM. The reporter also volunteered virtio networking and reproduction across multiple access networks and target servers; IPv4 and IPv6 reproduction was added by the reporter in c17. The tuning result from c2 is retained as volunteered information.

question_patterns: Since the tuning did not change the symptom, can you capture the lower-level QUIC trace for a failed handshake?
What raw QUIC parsing messages appear during one of the timeouts?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: My attached QUIC trace includes 'qc_parse_pkt_frms(): leaving on error' and then 'packet parsing failed -> dropped' for an Initial packet with pn=2.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: There are no parsing failures or dropped Initial packets in my trace; HAProxy sends its full handshake response and the client stops replying.

edges.comment: Recovery from the reporter's c2 tuning attempt into the diagnostic request from c3-c4. All facts describe the reporter's deployment and traces.

question_patterns: Can you temporarily disable UDP segmentation offload in HAProxy and repeat the curl loop?
Please run a config-toggle test for UDP GSO and tell me whether the timeout frequency changes.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I disabled UDP GSO and repeated the curl test, but it still hangs intermittently.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: After disabling UDP GSO I cannot reproduce a single timeout, and enabling it again immediately brings the hangs back.

question_patterns: Does an affected browser still hang if HTTP/3 is temporarily disabled?
Can an affected Windows user turn off HTTP/3 as a diagnostic test and report whether the connection hangs continue?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: One of our affected Firefox 143.0.4 users disabled QUIC completely and has not seen the hanging connections since. I attached a screenshot of the Firefox setting used for that test.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The same connections still hang with HTTP/3 disabled and HTTP/2 in use.
Disabling HTTP/3 avoids the hangs in Edge as well as Firefox.

edges.comment: Reporter c15 and c17-c19, on the reporter's service and an affected Freifunk Munich user's Firefox installation. Both are handler-directed configuration probes, so they are measurements rather than final solutions. The affected browser user is folded into the simulated user side.

question_patterns: Can you test a different prebuilt curl binary locally and remotely to see whether the client build affects reproduction?
Please compare the failing client with the supplied static builds on localhost, nearby hosts, and the original remote endpoint.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried the supplied curl 8.16.0 static build on localhost, a host in the same rack, and a farther-away host, and I could not reproduce it. The supplied macOS arm64 build also did not reproduce it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every supplied static build reproduces the same timeout at roughly the same rate, including on localhost.

question_patterns: Can you build comparable curl variants with different QUIC backends and report which binaries reproduce the timeout?
Please vary the client QUIC backend while keeping the curl and TLS library versions as close as possible.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I built curl 8.16.0 with OpenSSL 3.5.2 and --with-ngtcp2. That binary uses ngtcp2 1.16.0 and nghttp3 1.12.0, and it reproduces the issue.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The ngtcp2 build completes every attempt, while only the alternative backend build hangs.
The ngtcp2 build reproduces less frequently, but still produces the same handshake timeout.

question_patterns: What happens with the otherwise comparable client built against the alternative QUIC backend?
Does changing only the curl QUIC backend alter the outcome?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: When I compile the comparable curl build with --with-openssl-quic instead of ngtcp2, I cannot reproduce the timeout.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Both backend variants reproduce the timeout identically.

edges.comment: Reporter c21 and c27 on the reporter's systems: raw results from supplied and custom-built curl binaries. The conclusion about fragmented CRYPTO frames exhausting HAProxy's buffer is engineer-side and is introduced by e6.

solution.intent: Replace the existing non-contiguous QUIC CRYPTO buffer with the initial ncbuf2 implementation so extremely fragmented Initial CRYPTO data can be buffered without exhausting the gap representation.
solution.concrete_example: Deploy the development branch containing ncbuf2 on a test HAProxy host and stress it with the repeatedly failing HTTP/3 curl client before considering a broader rollout.
solution.inference_hint: Engineers combined the raw parser-drop trace with controlled ngtcp2 reproduction and HAProxy instrumentation. They concluded that aggressively fragmented Initial CRYPTO frames created many tiny holes, causing ncb_add or qc_handle_crypto_frm to fail when the old ncbuf exhausted its gap representation. The reporter did not derive that internal mechanism from the trace.

edges.comment: Participant4 and participant7 c32-c43 proposed the ncbuf redesign; reporter c44-c47 deployed the ncbuf2 development branch and observed that the original hangs disappeared. Participant7 c48 then reported a separate roughly 1% CRYPTO_ERROR under burst testing, so this initial implementation was superseded and is a known blind path as the final production fix.

solution.intent: Replace the superseded ncbuf2 candidate with the corrected ncbmbuf implementation and validate it across the real HAProxy deployment and affected browsers.
solution.concrete_example: Roll out the updated ncbmbuf development branch, repeat the curl stress loop, and collect feedback from the Firefox and Edge users who previously experienced hangs.

edges.comment: Participant7 c48 supplied the corrected ncbmbuf branch after finding a separate error in ncbuf2. Reporter c49-c50 rolled it out to all of the reporter's machines and relayed operational results plus feedback from the previously affected Firefox and Edge users, folded into the simulated user side.

solution.intent: Ship the corrected ncbmbuf-based QUIC fix so HAProxy can buffer aggressively fragmented Initial CRYPTO frames without dropping the handshake.
solution.concrete_example: Merge the corrected ncbmbuf implementation and switch QUIC CRYPTO buffering to it after the real-world deployment has completed repeated curl and browser verification.
solution.inference_hint: The final accepted diagnosis is that aggressive CRYPTO-frame fragmentation can create more fine-grained holes than HAProxy's old ncbuf can represent, causing Initial packet parsing to fail and the packet to be dropped. The corrected bitmap-backed ncbmbuf removes that internal limitation. This conclusion was established by maintainers using the reporter's traces, controlled clients, and HAProxy instrumentation.

edges.comment: Participant7 c51 reports that the corrected ncbmbuf implementation and associated QUIC fix were merged after reporter c50 confirmed stable operation and no reproducible Firefox or Edge hangs. The later statement that it would not be backported to 2.6 is release coordination and is not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the final accepted root cause: aggressively fragmented QUIC Initial CRYPTO frames create too many small holes for HAProxy's old non-contiguous buffer representation, causing CRYPTO insertion or parsing to fail and Initial packets to be dropped until the client reaches ERR_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the collected evidence: HAProxy's raw packet-parsing failure, reproduction with the ngtcp2-backed client but not the comparable OpenSSL-QUIC client, and successful real-world testing of the corrected buffer implementation.
The final fix must use the corrected ncbmbuf-based QUIC buffering implementation and preserve HTTP/3; disabling HTTP/3 is only a temporary diagnostic workaround.
Must not recommend QUIC loss/reorder tuning or disabling UDP GSO as the fix, because both were tested without changing the curl hangs.
Must not treat the initial ncbuf2 development branch as the final fix, because maintainers found a separate burst-triggered CRYPTO_ERROR and replaced it with the corrected ncbmbuf implementation.
Must require verification with repeated curl requests and affected Firefox or Edge users on a build containing the corrected fix before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced network and infrastructure operator who administers HAProxy across multiple points of presence, captures packet and application traces, builds curl with alternate QUIC backends, changes HAProxy tuning, and canary-deploys development builds under real traffic.
persona_hint.communication_style: Highly cooperative and technically detailed; supplies commands, versions, traces, and production observations; eagerly tests hypotheses while clearly stating when a result is only suggestive.
